key_insight: MMFlash investigates faster speculative decoding for vision-language models by examining how much each generated token depends on visual input. It introduces a KL-divergence metric to measure that dependence; the provided abstract is truncated before the main findings.
problem_solved: Diffusion-based speculative decoding has primarily focused on text-only tasks, leaving unclear how visual information affects token drafting and verification in multimodal generation.
method: Study multimodal speculative decoding, where a lightweight drafter proposes tokens for parallel verification by a target vision-language model.
Build on the diffusion-drafting setting exemplified by DFlash, which proposes an entire token block in one forward pass.
Measure token-level visual dependence using KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input.
impact: This work could help practitioners understand when visual context matters for efficient token drafting. Specific MMFlash design details and measured speedups are not available in the provided excerpt.

paper_title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Sicheng Feng, Zigeng Chen, Song Wang, Gongfan Fang, Xinchao Wang
